what_this_is: Every 'X and colleagues' or 'X et al.' on the page, with a record that somebody opened the author list and checked that X is the first author. This file exists because issue two published 'Jacot and colleagues' from a gate summary while in the middle of fixing an attribution gap. The paper is by Tanguy and colleagues. A name is the one thing on a page that a reader cannot check against context — it either matches the byline or it does not.

THE_REVIEW_MISDESCRIBED_THIS_PAPER.what_the_review_says: 32 radiology residents; sensitivity up 12 percentage points from 0.73 to 0.85 (P < 0.01); mean reading time down 18% from 68s to 56s; performance stable at a three-month follow-up with specificity around 0.80.
THE_REVIEW_MISDESCRIBED_THIS_PAPER.what_the_paper_says: EIGHT radiologists in training — four first-year, four third-year. 150 chest X-rays, 50 in each of three conditions: no AI, AI on demand, AI integrated into the reporting system. The AI is BS-Net, providing regional severity scores with confidence levels and explainability maps. The outcomes are mean absolute error against a consensus gold standard and inter-rater agreement, which rose from an intraclass correlation of 0.665 without AI to 0.813 with it integrated. Residents requested AI in 70% of cases and overrode it when its errors exceeded an acceptability threshold. NO THREE-MONTH FOLLOW-UP EXISTS IN THE PAPER. No sensitivity, specificity or reading-time figures are reported for the residents.
THE_REVIEW_MISDESCRIBED_THIS_PAPER.how_bad_this_was_going_to_be: We had built a paragraph on the review's version and given it prominence as the null result the piece was honour-bound to carry as loudly as the positive one. It would have published. The only reason it did not is that lint_claims blocks any 'X and colleagues' with no record that somebody opened the author list — a check built after issue two published 'Jacot and colleagues'. Opening the author list meant opening the paper.
THE_REVIEW_MISDESCRIBED_THIS_PAPER.confidence: The byline, the count of eight, the three-condition design and the ICC figures are structural facts from the publisher's own page. We are confident the paper is not what the review describes. We are NOT asserting how the review's figures arose, and the page does not speculate.

the_rule: A name on the page is checked against the paper's own byline, not against a reference list in a third document. Two of the twelve here are not, and both are flagged. Either they get opened before publication or the sentences lose the names.
what_this_check_caught: On 30 August 2026 this file's own requirement — that a name be checked against the paper's byline — forced us to open two papers we had only read about. One matched its summary exactly. The other did not match it in the number of participants, the design, the outcome measures, or the existence of the follow-up the summary's whole value to us depended on. The check was built to stop a wrong surname reaching a page. It stopped a wrong study.
_schema_note: lint_claims matches the FIRST WORD of each 'X and colleagues' on the page against the `name` field in `verified`, and only counts an entry when `checked_against` is filled. The rich record below stays under `attributions`; `verified` is the machine-readable half. Both are maintained by hand and both must agree.
